races.name: A McKie Builders EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Beechwood Glory
runners_data.note: Only two runs, both on Good ground over 6f at a similar level, finishing 5-3; the experience edge over several debutants here is modest but real, and a prominent or mid-division style suits this race shape well.

runners_data.name: Coul Blue
runners_data.note: Ran 4th over 7f on Good last time for Michael Dods, who has been in solid form (3 from 27 in 14 days); a genuine hold-up type who wants the pace to be honest, and should be closer to her natural rear position than some rivals.

runners_data.name: Flashing Star
runners_data.note: Two outings both over 5f on Soft or Standard, so this step up to 6f on Good is an unproven combination; the headgear flag (h) is worth noting, and 42 days off means Mark Walford has had time to school her before this assignment.

runners_data.name: Lone Striker
runners_data.note: Racecourse debut with no form string or last-run data, running style genuinely unknown — Phillip Makin has been selective with entries (1 from 6 in 14 days) which may indicate confidence, but there is nothing to anchor a positional read.

runners_data.name: Mick's The Boy
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with three runs on Good, including a runner-up over this exact course and distance; uncontested lead is his primary asset today, though his OR of 66 against the 120-rated band suggests raw ability is the limiting factor.

runners_data.name: Ponte Carlo
runners_data.note: Five runs of experience including course form over 6f Good (finished 5th and 6th) give him a tactical edge; a true hold-up horse by nature who has been pushed into the midfield map due to congestion at the rear — discount his chance if the shape requires him to close from off the pace against type.

runners_data.name: Redrosecastana
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Christopher Kellett, whose yard has had no winners from four runners in the last 14 days; no form or style data available, making positional assessment speculative.

runners_data.name: Unbeatable Fame
runners_data.note: Ran 6th and 7th in both starts over 5f on Good for Fahey, who has a modest recent strike rate; the step up to 6f could suit a hold-up type who found 5f sharp, but has yet to show she has the class to convert.

runners_data.name: Black Cuillin
runners_data.note: Three consecutive 4th-place finishes on Good going, all over 5-6f, show admirable consistency without a win — a true closer by nature whose redistribution to midfield in this map is a flag that she may not get the run of the race she needs.

runners_data.name: Roman Crystal
runners_data.note: The only confirmed prominent-style runner aside from the leader; four runs all on Good over 6f at Ayr, finishing 3-4-5-6, suggests course familiarity and a horse who knows its job, and tracking Mick's The Boy from the front is exactly his role.

races.paceDynamic: Mick's The Boy is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner maiden and, with no other genuine pace-presser to force the issue, Jake Dickson should be able to dictate an honest but uncontested tempo on Good ground over six furlongs at Ayr. Roman Crystal is the only confirmed prominent-style runner and will look to sit just off the leader's shoulder, creating a small pack at the head of affairs without triggering a suicidal sprint. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Ponte Carlo and Black Cuillin are genuine closers by nature but have been redistributed to midfield in the map because the true hold-up positions are already occupied; Coul Blue, Flashing Star, and Unbeatable Fame are the more authentic late runners likely to occupy those slots. This race shape — a single unhurried front-runner setting a controlled, sustainable pace — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or in mid-division and produce a decisive burst in the final two furlongs, making prominent and mid-division profiles the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mick's Boy Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Mick's The Boy dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the field settles into its natural order behind him, Roman Crystal tracks closest and the race becomes a test of late quality rather than raw stamina.
scenarios.body: Mick's The Boy's ability to control fractions without being pressured is the key; Roman Crystal, sat a length or two off the pace, is best placed to pounce, while mid-division horses who can travel comfortably will have first run on the closers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough — perhaps Roman Crystal pushes Mick's The Boy — and the field fans wide in the straight, horses held up in the early stages get a true test and can overhaul a weakening front group.
scenarios.body: Coul Blue and Flashing Star, both genuine hold-up types with form over further, would be aided by a quicker tempo that burns off the leaders in the final furlong; Unbeatable Fame has the profile to make late ground on fast-draining ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Mick's The Boy goes too slow and the field bunches, creating a sprint finish, an unexposed debutant or lightly-raced horse catches the field napping with a sharp early turn of foot.
scenarios.body: Lone Striker and Redrosecastana, both making their racecourse debuts with unknown styles, carry the widest upside here; either could possess a natural early zip that the field hasn't had to factor in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Ponte Carlo or Black Cuillin, despite being redistributed to midfield against their natural role, manage to push forward and secure a prominent pitch, they compete more effectively than their mapped position suggests.
scenarios.body: Both carry STYLE_FIT discounts precisely because racing out of role is a cost, but if the pace is moderate enough that prominent positions become available mid-race, Ponte Carlo's wider experience over this course-and-distance profile gives him a residual chance.

watchPoints.text: Mick's The Boy controls the early tempo unopposed — if Roman Crystal tracks aggressively and applies pressure, the front-runner's fragile OR of 66 versus a 120-rated field becomes exposed in the final furlong.

Ponte Carlo and Black Cuillin are both true hold-up types mapped to midfield against their nature — watch whether either can push forward at the start to reclaim a more suitable position, which would materially change their chance.
Lone Striker and Redrosecastana are both debut runners with no style or form data; if either shows natural speed and breaks sharply, they could disrupt the anticipated race shape entirely.

Good ground is confirmed for the 5:27 race specifically at Ayr — no going concern for the majority of runners, but Flashing Star's two starts both came on softer or artificial surfaces, making this her first genuine test on a quick top.

races.name: Sunday Roast At Western House Hotel Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hi Lord
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a course-and-distance win last time out (1/5f/GOO) and solid recent form; Jason McHugh partners for W H Harrison, who has no winners from five runners in the last 14 days, but the horse's own record on this going and trip is the key positive.|

runners_data.name: King Of The Jungle
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner, trained by Michael & David Easterby who are 2/27 in the last 14 days; has won twice at 5f including once on Good, but the style-fit flag (0.93) is a reminder he may find rivals tracking him more closely than his wider-draw races have allowed — watch for how cleanly he breaks.|

runners_data.name: Harb
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type partnered by apprentice Lexie Clarkson (7lb claim) for Tristan Davidson, who is 2/10 in the last 14 days; ran just seven days ago and showed a place last time at 5f/Good — the short turnaround and young claimer are factors to weigh against a consistent course profile.|

runners_data.name: Water Of Leith
runners_data.note: Deep hold-up specialist, eight years old and without a win from 15 similar-going runs (0W1P); Jim Goldie has two winners from 40 runners in the last 14 days and this horse's form string of 655365 suggests a place rather than a win is the ceiling here.|

runners_data.name: Startling
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with an outstanding place record (0W3P in last five on Good, including three seconds) who wears a hood; John Wainwright's yard is quiet (0/4, T14) but Startling's consistency at 5f on Good ground makes her a notable each-way interest for prominent finishers.|

runners_data.name: Midnight Lir
runners_data.note: A genuine deep closer by nature, but the field's excess of hold-up types means he is unlikely to get his preferred rearward position — wearing a tongue-tie and blinkers, Michael Dods sends him here 15 days after his last run; the style-fit flag (0.91) and redistribution reflect a real risk of being outpaced for position.|

runners_data.name: South Parade
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's five-year-old is another true hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield slot by the field's makeup; eight days between runs with Ethan Tindall (5lb) aboard, and a form string of 074963 that includes a previous course win — the style-fit (0.93) discount applies given he is unlikely to get his natural ground.|

runners_data.name: Harry Mole
runners_data.note: The field's second-most prominent horse and the one most likely to apply pressure to King Of The Jungle; Dougie Costello is a useful booking for Steph Hollinshead and Harry Mole's form of -05223 shows he hits the board at 5f on Good — if he slots in second, he is the natural each-way foil.|

runners_data.name: Keep The Gold
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type wearing a hood, trained by Michael Dods alongside stablemate Midnight Lir; form includes back-to-back seconds at 5f on Good, but a 33-day absence and redistribution to midfield (style-fit 0.93) temper confidence that he recaptures that level here.|

runners_data.name: Falcon Queen
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly who wears a hood and is a true closer in style — her record of 0W0P in the last seven runs on similar going is the most damning stat in the field; the redistribution into midfield (style-fit 0.90) compounds the challenge, and R Mike Smith's yard has only one winner from nine in the last fortnight.|

runners_data.name: Supremissy
runners_data.note: Won last time out (1/5f/GOO) for Iain Jardine, who is notably active with five winners from 27 runners in the last 14 days — the trainer angle is the strongest positive here; a 47-day absence is the query, and being a redistributed hold-up horse (style-fit 0.92) means she will need to find her position quickly to repeat that win.|

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse who wears a hood and is partnered by apprentice Shay Farmer (5lb); R Mike Smith sends him here alongside Falcon Queen, and a record of 2W4P from 15 similar-going runs shows more resilience than his recent form of 377565 implies — but at OR 46 and redistributed into midfield, he faces a stiff task.|

runners_data.name: Summerstorms Dream
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old has a form string of 357726 with no wins from 11 similar-going starts (0W2P); Lauren Young's 5lb claim is a small help but being a true closer bumped into a midfield map position (style-fit 0.90) means she will need everything to go right at the business end.|

races.paceDynamic: King Of The Jungle is the one confirmed front-runner in this field of 13 and, with no genuine rival looking to press him for the lead, he is likely to bowl along at a sustainable gallop from the outset over this straight 5f at Ayr on Good ground. Harry Mole is the only other horse with a prominent profile who could push forward and apply some pressure, but without a rival willing to go to war with King Of The Jungle, the pace is likely to be honest rather than frantic. The field behind him is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up types, yet the configuration is distorted — Midnight Lir, South Parade, Falcon Queen, Keep The Gold, Supremissy, Royal Duke, and Summerstorms Dream are all true hold-up horses who cannot all settle at the rear and are mapped into midfield positions they would not naturally occupy; the horses most likely to actually secure a midfield berth with cover are those with sharper gate speed among this group. A solo, unhurried front-runner on a flat, straight 5f on Good ground creates a shape that classically rewards horses racing prominently or just off the pace — the midfield hold-up brigade face the toughest task, as a moderate gallop will compress the finish and leave little time to reel in a front-runner who has preserved energy.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: King Of The Jungle Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If King Of The Jungle bounces out cleanly and sets a controlled, uncontested gallop that leaves rivals with too much ground to make up.
scenarios.body: King Of The Jungle races unchallenged in front, dictates his own fractions, and simply finds enough in the closing stages on Good ground before the hold-up horses can close; the flat, straight track means there is no bend to help closers eat into the deficit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Harry Mole hustles up to join King Of The Jungle and the two set a true pace, with a prominent racer picking up the pieces.
scenarios.body: The pace becomes more genuine as two horses share the front rank, draining the stamina of the leader but handing the race to a horse who has stalked the action from just off the pace; Hi Lord or Startling, both capable of finishing from a tracking position, are best placed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and horses who have been shuffled into midfield manage to thread through a tiring field in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Some of the redistributed hold-up types — Harb or Water Of Leith — get a cleaner passage than expected and run on into a contest that has been run at an uneven gallop; however, this scenario is tempered because most of the supposed closers are not genuine deep hold-up horses and the flat track offers limited late-race advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes crowding from an early stage, disrupting the front-runner's rhythm and scrambling the race order entirely.
scenarios.body: Interference or a false start disrupts the shape, creating gaps that allow an unconsidered runner such as Supremissy or South Parade to slip through unnoticed; these horses carry discounted chances given their redistributed positions and style-fit flags, but in a chaotic shape they are live at a big price.

watchPoints.text: King Of The Jungle — watch his gate and the first furlong: if he breaks cleanly and clears by two lengths inside the first furlong with no Harry Mole pressure, the race is likely his to lose from the front.

Harry Mole — the critical pressure horse; if Dougie Costello elects to push forward and sit on King Of The Jungle's shoulder from the outset, the pace dynamic shifts materially and the hold-up horses move from outsiders to genuine contenders.

Supremissy — Iain Jardine's 14-day strike rate of 5/27 is the best trainer angle in the race and she arrives on the back of a win; monitor market moves, as stable confidence could elevate her despite the redistribution concern.

Startling — three consecutive placed efforts at 5f on Good, wears a hood; if this race develops into a searching gallop, her consistent finishing profile makes her a horse to keep safe regardless of the exact scenario that unfolds.

Crowding risk in the early stages — with 13 runners over a straight 5f and the majority of hold-up types unable to get their natural position, the first two furlongs carry an elevated risk of interference; horses drawn wide may get a cleaner run than those trapped on the rail.

races.name: Book Ladbrokes Ayr Gold Cup Ladies Day Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Tiger
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a recent course win over 10f on good ground — lightly weighted at 147lbs relative to OR, and Ryan Kavanagh's 3lb claim is useful; six days since last run is no concern and similar-going form of 4 from 10 shows consistency.|

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: Last-time-out placed over 17f on good going suggests stamina is no issue at 1m2f but the step back in trip is a question; Andrew Mullen rides and the horse has placed on good ground four times from 15 runs, though winless at this level — 21 days since last run is fresh.|

runners_data.name: Draupnir
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with Billy Garritty up for the Easterbys; three recent placings on good ground at 9f suggest this step to 1m2f is a slight concern, but he is the most likely horse to push Faeberon for the lead and his T14 strike rate (2/27) offers little trainer confidence.|

runners_data.name: Geo
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type whose true role is at the rear, here mapped to midfield due to the congested field; strong form at 8-11f on good going (14 from 15 sim-going runs) with Paul Mulrennan aboard — style fit is compromised, which tempers expectations despite solid recent form.|

runners_data.name: Pol Roger
runners_data.note: A patient hold-up performer in reality, though shown in midfield here given how many closers are in this race; has placed on good ground at 10f twice recently and Sean Kirrane partners — the redistribution means he may not get the run he needs.|

runners_data.name: Dryburgh
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with Sam James up and three places from six good-ground runs; 64 days off the track is the key concern here, and the headgear flag (h) notes a previous hood — if sharp enough, his 1m2f good-ground form reads well.|

runners_data.name: Unchartedterritory
runners_data.note: Last won over 9f on soft going for David O'Meara with Lewis Edmunds claiming 3lbs; 60 days off is a fitness question, and form on good going is moderate (0W1P from 4 runs) — an each-way profile at best unless O'Meara has prepared him well for this return.|

runners_data.name: Faeberon
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner whose style fit is slightly diluted (0.93) as a natural prominent type here asked to fully lead — last won over 10f on standard going, Dougie Costello rides, and 41 days off should mean he arrives fresh; the single real pace factor in the race.|

runners_data.name: Mayor Of Maghera
runners_data.note: Won over 9f on good ground most recently for R Mike Smith and has placed at similar distances; a true hold-up horse shown in midfield due to redistribution, and James Sullivan will need to make this work from a position that may not be natural — the 0.92 style fit is a real concern.|

runners_data.name: Natzor
runners_data.note: A fader in finishes per the system flag, and history of finishing 8th-12th on good ground (0 wins, 0 places in 15 sim-going runs) tells a stark story; Barry McHugh rides for Lizzie Quinlan whose T14 is blank — the redistribution to midfield further compresses an already fragile prospect.|

runners_data.name: Phantom Shadow
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with Jason Hart who has genuinely progressive form — last two runs produced a win and a place over 10f on good going, and his style fit, though redistributed to midfield, is among the better hold-up profiles here; Whillans is a sharp small-yard trainer worth noting.|

runners_data.name: Path To Peace
runners_data.note: Has finished 6th, 10th and 9th in three career starts — all at distances of 10-12f on good or soft — and the fades-in-finish flag reinforces limited confidence; Greg Fairley takes the mount and a tongue-tie is recorded (tb), suggesting the trainer is searching for improvement.|

runners_data.name: Annandale
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old for Jim Goldie who is reliable in the 3rd-4th zone on good ground at 11-13f (5 runs, 1W3P); Lauren Young's 5lb claim keeps the weight manageable, but the redistribution from natural hold-up position, combined with age, reduces upside even in a well-run race.|

runners_data.name: Ibn Altheeb
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with Jack Nicholls claiming 3lbs for Iain Jardine; a tongue-tie (b) is worn and recent form is modest (4th best finish), though there is a placing on good ground at 11f — redistributed from natural hold-up to midfield, which with a low OR of 66 limits his scope.|

races.paceDynamic: Faeberon is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and should dictate comfortably from the front at a sustainable gallop on good ground over 1m2f at Ayr, with Draupnir the only genuine prominent challenger likely to push him. With no genuine pace pressure anticipated, Faeberon can control tempo and shape the contest entirely to suit a waiting style in the straight — but a soft, uncontested lead also risks setting up a race where the field arrives in a bunch late. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the map can physically accommodate at the rear: Geo, Pol Roger, Phantom Shadow, Mayor Of Maghera, and several others are true wait-and-pounce types who will be jostling for the same midfield to rear positions. This race shape — a single front-runner at a controlled pace — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or close the gap in one smooth run from midfield, as the genuine deep hold-up horses will be squeezed for position and may not find the clear passage a truly strong pace would provide.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Faeberon Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Faeberon leads at a fair but unhurried pace and no rival forces the tempo, allowing him to dictate throughout.
scenarios.body: Faeberon, suited to leading and last-time-out winner, builds a rhythm from the front and Dougie Costello steals a march turning in, with the field unable to reel him in off too gentle a gallop. Horses who travel prominently like Draupnir are best positioned to capitalise if Faeberon fades, while most hold-up types arrive too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Faeberon sets a genuinely honest gallop that stretches the field, allowing the best-travelling midfielders to sweep through in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The moderate pace gives way to a strong finishing burst as horses like Phantom Shadow and Geo, who have been finding to finish in recent form, arrive with purpose through the field. Horses with strong recent form at the distance and on good ground — Tiger and Unchartedterritory — are best placed to exploit gaps.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Finish Late
scenarios.trigger: If Faeberon goes too fast early and sets a true end-to-end gallop that causes the field to string out and create space for genuine closers.
scenarios.body: A strong pace would suit the backmarkers for once, but the risk is that most supposed hold-up horses in this field are redistributed and not truly comfortable sitting last — so even in this scenario, their natural positions are compromised. Mr Lincoln and Dryburgh, who have been placed at this sort of trip on good going from off the pace, are the most credible late finishers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Faeberon and Draupnir push each other hard in front and the contest becomes a genuine duel between the two, burning off the midfield before the turn.
scenarios.body: Both front-runners are left exposed racing keenly, and one tiring leader hands it to the other or creates a gap for an immediately following horse. Draupnir's form on good going and Faeberon's course experience make them the primary beneficiaries if the race degenerates into an early battle.

watchPoints.text: Faeberon faces zero genuine pace pressure — watch whether Dougie Costello uses this to set a dawdle that turns the race into a sprint finish and negates hold-up runners entirely.

The majority of the field — Geo, Pol Roger, Phantom Shadow, Mayor Of Maghera, Path To Peace, Annandale, Ibn Altheeb — are all natural hold-up types competing for the same rear positions; watch for traffic problems and interference in the straight as they converge simultaneously.

Phantom Shadow's recent form (win and place in last two at 10f on good going) makes him the most dangerous of the redistributed closers — watch whether Jason Hart can find a clear path from a compromised position.
Dryburgh and Unchartedterritory both return from 60+ day absences — watch market moves at the track as an indicator of stable confidence before the off.

Tiger's course win over 10f on good ground six days ago flags fitness and track affinity — watch whether Ryan Kavanagh elects to ride closer to the pace than usual given how the race is likely to be run.

races.name: Unite Ewing Hope's Happy Retirement Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hale End
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for Michael Dods who has placed twice at this trip on good going recently; blinkers on and only 19 days since last run, sharp and fit; sits in the sweet spot just off the likely pace battle between Milteye and High Point.|

runners_data.name: Count Palatine
runners_data.note: Stablemate of Hale End, off 57 days which is the biggest concern here; has placed on good ground at this trip but recent form at 7f suggests the mile is preferred; Sean Kirrane will need to find a clean passage from a prominent position.|

runners_data.name: Jannas Journey
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Jim Goldie who clearly stays the mile well and won over this course and distance on good ground last time; Lauren Young's 5lb claim is valuable and the wide-open Ayr straight suits a horse that can motor late.|

runners_data.name: Military Leader
runners_data.note: In excellent recent form with a sequence of placed efforts, but this field's prominent congestion means Phillip Makin's runner is unlikely to get its favoured position just off the pace and will likely find itself deeper than ideal; the style-fit discount is real but the underlying form is strong.|

runners_data.name: Milteye
runners_data.note: One of two confirmed front-runners; showed she can dominate when allowed to bowl along in front, winning on soft but her good-going record over 8f at this track (one win from four on Good) is modest; Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim and 50 days off are factors to weigh.|

runners_data.name: Breakdancer
runners_data.note: Consistent for the Crisford team, well placed on RPR and only 12 days fresh; has placed in three of his last five on good ground over 8f and Paul Mulrennan's experience in a congested field is an asset from a prominent position.|

runners_data.name: High Point
runners_data.note: Co-pace-setter but his recent distance form is all over 10f-16f which raises a serious question about his stamina-speed mix over a flat mile; Andrew Mullen will likely push him forward from the off but he may find the shorter trip tests him late.|

runners_data.name: Theoryofeverything
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner in the field but has gone winless in his last five, all on good ground at 8f; Jason Hart knows how to drop him in from the hold-up position and the honest pace suits his style, though his form figures suggest he just misses rather than wins.|

runners_data.name: Walsingham
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's runner has the best good-going winning record in this field with three wins from eight on Good at 8f; Billy Garritty can sit prominent or just off the pace and the horse is only 8 days since his last run, so freshness is not a concern.|

runners_data.name: Bravais
runners_data.note: Longest absent runner here at 92 days off, which is a significant fitness query despite Ian Williams having a strong strike rate overall; hold-up style suits this scenario but the layoff and uninspiring recent form (five consecutive finishes outside the placings) make him a speculative inclusion.|

races.paceDynamic: Milteye and High Point are the two confirmed front-runners and will go head-to-head for the lead from the off, creating a genuinely contested pace over Ayr's flat mile on good ground. Behind them, Hale End, Count Palatine, Breakdancer, and Walsingham all want prominent positions, generating a congested early order that will see horses shuffled and squeezed between the two-furlong and three-furlong markers. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position — Milteye and High Point are most likely to actually get to the front, with Military Leader the runner most likely to be forced back from its natural role. This contested pace on a flat, galloping track that typically rewards sustained galloping types gives the clearest edge to strong-finishing hold-up horses and genuine mid-to-late movers, provided the leaders don't collapse catastrophically and hand it to an opportunist from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Milteye and High Point push each other along at a genuine clip and set an honest gallop that stretches the field turning for home.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn each other off and the race sets up perfectly for Jannas Journey, Theoryofeverything, and Bravais to pick up late ground down the Ayr straight; the flat mile with no undulation means stamina and a well-timed run count more than anything else.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest but not suicidal, leaving a prominent tracker to cruise into the lead two furlongs out without spending energy fighting for position.
scenarios.body: Hale End or Breakdancer, sitting just behind the pace battle, time their move to hit the front as the leaders fade and sustain to the line; both have the fitness and the form at this trip on good ground to be dangerous from this slot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Steals It Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is more controlled than it appears and one of the front-runners is allowed to dictate a moderate tempo before kicking clear.
scenarios.body: Milteye, the more proven front-runner of the pair, is best placed to exploit this if High Point fails to push on and settles the race into a falsely run affair; Milteye's win record when making the running and the flat Ayr straight make this a live threat.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Squeeze, Traffic Victims
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes significant interference two to three furlongs out and a midfield horse finds a clear run late.
scenarios.body: Military Leader, racing out of its natural prominent role and pushed deeper into the field, would need everything to fall right to deliver from this disadvantaged position; Walsingham and Count Palatine could also benefit if gaps appear, though all three face messy traffic in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Milteye and High Point are both confirmed front-runners — watch the first two furlongs for how aggressively each jockey commits, as a full-on speed duel at the top could leave both weakened by the home turn, dramatically opening the race for closers.

Prominent congestion between Hale End, Count Palatine, Breakdancer, Walsingham, and the displaced Military Leader creates a genuine traffic flashpoint at the 2-3 furlong marker — any horse caught in a pocket or forced wide could lose critical lengths at the business end.

High Point's recent runs have all been at trips between 12f and 16f; if he cannot sustain his early pace over the shorter 8f trip, he may capitulate quickly in the home straight and cause interference to horses tracking him.

Walsingham is the most course-and-distance proven runner in the field on this going type — if Billy Garritty slots him just off the contested lead without getting caught in the prominent scrum, he becomes a dangerous mid-race mover to track.|

Bravais returns after 92 days off and should be monitored in the parade ring for condition; if visually sharp, the hold-up style could suit a pace-set race, but the layoff combined with flat recent form makes him a watch rather than a lean.|

races.name: Christmas Parties At Western House Hotel Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mr Cool
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Charlie Johnston who recorded a win and two places in his last five on good ground at 6f; with five 6f good-ground runs from 15 and a positive style fit for this race, he is the key pace influence and holds a strong tactical advantage dictating unchallenged.

runners_data.name: Annie Edson Taylor
runners_data.note: Phillip Makin's five-year-old has a course-and-distance win in recent form and solid record on good ground (6/15 sim-going), though 52 days off the track is a mild concern; a natural hold-up horse who needs things to go wrong for the leader to get involved.

runners_data.name: Impressor
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type for Phillip Makin wearing a p headgear; his sim-going record on good is modest (5/15, 0W2P) and form figures of 400636 suggest he needs a strongly-run race that this pace map is unlikely to provide.

runners_data.name: Kelpie Grey
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan takes the ride on this Jim Goldie six-year-old who has modest recent form (658606) but is mapped to a prominent position and could at least track Mr Cool; form on good ground at 6f is 0W3P from 8 runs, suggesting placed threats rather than winner's capability.

runners_data.name: Thunderstorm Katie
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose true style has been redistributed to midfield due to the volume of closers in this field — she'll likely race closer than preferred but her 1W5P record in sim-going conditions and recent placed runs at 5f show she carries ability; the style mismatch dampens her chance in this shape.

runners_data.name: Taaklam
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type for Harriet Bethell, last seen 8 days ago; sim-going record is thin (2/8, 0W0P) and his best form has come on Standard surfaces rather than good turf, raising a soft going preference query for this outing.

runners_data.name: Masai Angel
runners_data.note: Fahey-trained three-year-old whose natural hold-up style puts her at a disadvantage in this shape — she'll be carried into a midfield position she wouldn't choose, and her limited good-ground sim-going record (2/4) adds uncertainty; form of 5-430 on good suggests she's yet to fulfil her early promise at this level.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Kisses
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type for R Mike Smith with back-to-back thirds on good ground at 6f in recent starts; 0W3P in sim-going suggests consistent placed efforts but a lack of winning punch, and without a hot pace she may not get close enough to threaten.

runners_data.name: Elemma
runners_data.note: Another Fahey hold-up runner whose positioning on the map has been pushed forward by the volume of closers — her last four runs are on good or good-to-soft at 6-7f and she's yet to win or place in the sim-going band; true style likely to leave her further back than ideal.

runners_data.name: Highfield Sunshine
runners_data.note: John & Sean Quinn's four-year-old has a strong sim-going record (8/15) and reasonable placed form (0W4P), but her natural hold-up style means she's mapped into midfield against her instincts; no wins since a maiden, and the 17-day gap since last run is fine but she needs pace to aim at.

runners_data.name: Ukiyo
runners_data.note: Andrew Kinirons's five-year-old comes here 50 days fresh with a win and three places in sim-going conditions but his best result (15/6f/GOO) highlights inconsistency; a genuine hold-up type shifted into midfield by the race shape, and the trainer's 0/5 in the last 14 days is an additional flag.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old wears a visor and has a win at 6f on good ground in recent form (1/6f/GOO) with three additional places in sim-going; a natural hold-up type mapped forward due to redistribution, but his versatility and course experience make him the most dangerous of the hold-up horses if the pace collapses.

runners_data.name: Lanarra
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for R Mike Smith who brings a form string of 1-2343, showing consistent placed form on good ground at 6f; a natural hold-up horse who needs things to unravel for the leader, but her recent consistency and light weight (120lbs) make her one of the more credible threats from the chasing pack.

races.paceDynamic: Mr Cool is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no rival genuinely equipped or positioned to press him hard from the off, he is set to control the tempo from the front on his own terms over this straight 6f at Ayr on good ground. Kelpie Grey is the only other horse mapped to a prominent position, but his recent form figures of 658606 suggest he lacks the gate speed or class to threaten Mr Cool's lead, leaving the pace effectively uncontested. The field behind Mr Cool is dominated by hold-up types — Annie Edson Taylor, Impressor, Taaklam, Whiskey Kisses, Doon The Glen, Ukiyo and Lanarra are all genuine closers — but with so many forced to race against their nature, the realistic pace picture behind the leader is muddled rather than organised. This field holds significantly more hold-up horses than can all find space at the rear, with Masai Angel, Thunderstorm Katie, Elemma, Highfield Sunshine and Ukiyo among the redistriubted hold-up types most likely to end up closer to midfield than they'd prefer, further compressing the chasing pack. A lone pace-setter dictating a sustainable gallop on good ground at Ayr heavily favours a front-running or prominent profile, with hold-up horses requiring either a strongly-run pace or a particularly powerful finishing effort to overhaul a controlling leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mr Cool Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Cool travels smoothly to the front and meets no serious challenge for the lead through the first two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Mr Cool dictates from flagfall, setting a measured but sustainable tempo that makes it extremely difficult for closers to close the gap on good ground; the straight 6f layout at Ayr with no pace pressure gives him every opportunity to conserve energy and quicken when asked.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Cool goes off too fast or ties up in the final furlong, allowing the trailing hold-up horses to pick him off late.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected early pace from Mr Cool burns him out in the closing stages, opening the door for the genuine hold-up horses who have settled off the pace to unleash their finishing runs; Annie Edson Taylor, who won over this course and distance last time, and Lanarra, consistent in recent form, are best positioned to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Squeeze, Prominent Horse Profits
scenarios.trigger: If the compacted midfield group creates interference or traffic issues, allowing a horse who secured a clean prominent pitch to coast through.
scenarios.body: With so many horses forced into a compressed chasing pack, a horse who manages to slot just behind Mr Cool without being caught in the scrum has a clear passage down the straight; Kelpie Grey and Thunderstorm Katie, if she gets closer than her natural style suggests, benefit most from this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Find Rail, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If a strong pace develops and the closers who secure the rail or an unobstructed outside run produce a mass late challenge.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the unlikely combination of Mr Cool setting a genuine strong gallop and several hold-up horses finding clear daylight simultaneously; Doon The Glen, with a recent course win, and Whiskey Kisses, who has shown consistent placed efforts on good ground, are the most plausible beneficiaries if this fragmented shape materialises.

watchPoints.text: Mr Cool's early sectionals are critical — if he idles in front without pressure, this race shape becomes very difficult to overcome for all hold-up horses; watch for any sign of him being allowed to bowl along at his own pace unchallenged in the opening two furlongs.

The sheer volume of hold-up horses (nine of thirteen runners) mapped into midfield creates a significant risk of traffic congestion in the straight — watch for Lanarra, Whiskey Kisses and Doon The Glen being caught in traffic and failing to find a clear run.

Doon The Glen wears a visor and has a recent win at 6f on good going at this course — his Jim Goldie trainer angle (2/40 in 14 days) is modest, but his course-and-distance profile makes him the most dangerous closer if Mr Cool stops.

Thunderstorm Katie's redistribution to midfield means she races out of her natural hold-up role — Lauren Young (5) claiming 5lbs could influence positioning, and it's worth monitoring whether she settles in behind the midfield group or gets pushed even further forward in running.

Annie Edson Taylor returns after 52 days off for Phillip Makin, who is 1/6 in the last 14 days; the tongue-tie is retained and her course-and-distance win is significant form, but the layoff combined with a pace map that doesn't suit hold-up horses is a double hurdle to clear.

races.name: Book The Ladbrokes Ayr Gold Cup Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Stoic Poet
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 3yo ridden by M.P. Sheehy, returning after 64 days off the track — form figures of 2/7f/SOF suggest he handles soft better than Good, and his hold-up style on a compressed pace scenario gives him little tactical room; similar-going form of 0W0P in two runs is the critical flag.

runners_data.name: Milford Grange
runners_data.note: Billy Garritty rides this Easterby-trained 3yo who has run second three times at 6-7f on soft and good — his natural hold-up style means he will be racing closer to the pace than ideal in a field this congested, tempering confidence that he can reproduce those placed efforts.

runners_data.name: Supreme Clarets
runners_data.note: Warren Fentiman takes the 3lb claim on this Fahey runner who has a strong record of placing at 7-8f on Good going, with three placed efforts in his last eight; his true hold-up profile is compromised by a crowded rear, though he has the form ceiling to trouble the judges if he threads through.

runners_data.name: Yaaser
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old for Jim Goldie who only ran seven days ago, with placed form at 7f on Good across seven runs — his natural hold-up style is squeezed by a packed field, and at OR 58 he is the lowest-rated runner here, making his task doubly difficult.

runners_data.name: Tap Dancer
runners_data.note: Andrew Mullen partners this Jim Goldie-trained 4yo who has placed at 7f Good before but also has runs over 10f suggesting he may stay further than this optimum trip; his hold-up style, forced closer by the field, and a career record of 0W2P on this going makes him harder to place in a winning narrative.

runners_data.name: Yy Spirit
runners_data.note: Lexie Clarkson's 7lb claim and 99 days off the track are the headline facts for Susan Corbett's 3yo, who has winning form over 6f on Standard and lost form figures on Soft; hold-up style and a 10-week absence make confidence difficult, though the claim is a practical positive if fitness holds.

runners_data.name: Sanafi Zabeel
runners_data.note: [Duplicate entry — see above; data already covered.]

runners_data.name: Circle Of Trust
runners_data.note: Lewis Edmunds takes the ride on Kevin Ryan's 3yo, winner over 7f on Soft and placed at 7f on Soft twice; headgear (blinkers) listed and form on Good ground is underwhelming at 9th and 10th, though his natural hold-up style will see him arriving late in a race where deep closers are structurally disadvantaged.

runners_data.name: Ubetterseethis
runners_data.note: Sam James partners this Craig Lidster 3yo who has placed form at 7-8f including wins and placed efforts on Soft — his form on Good is patchy (19th last time on Good), and 57 days off the track adds uncertainty to whether he can reproduce his best hold-up performances.

runners_data.name: Highfield Viking
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed prominent racer in this field beyond the two front-runners; Jason Hart takes the ride for Quinn, he has placed form at 7f on Good and the blinkers have been applied, making him the most naturally positioned horse to exploit the pace duel between the two leaders.

runners_data.name: Runninsonofagun
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Tristan Davidson, won over 8f on Good recently and has strong placed form at the trip; will look to dictate and has the fitness edge on just 12 days' rest, making him the primary pace-setter to assess throughout.

runners_data.name: Black Storm
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's 5yo carries headgear (blinkers) and Greg Fairley rides — his form shows consistent placing at 7f including 2nd on Good recently, and he is one of the more credible hold-up types despite being pushed forward by field congestion; the 30-day gap to his last run is manageable.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Of Dreams
runners_data.note: Dougie Costello rides for Quinn but this 5yo has been off 102 days and all recent form is on Standard (AW) going, making Good turf a significant unknown; his headgear (hood) and hold-up profile, forced into midfield, combine with the layoff and going uncertainty to make him the most opaque runner in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Runninsonofagun and Sanafi Zabeel are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead from the gates, creating a genuine and honest gallop over Ayr's 7f on Good ground — neither is a soft-lead type who will concede without a fight. With two genuine pace horses pressing each other through the first two furlongs, the race is likely to be run at a true tempo that tests stamina from the turn, setting up a surface that favours horses travelling efficiently just off the pace rather than those hunting from deep. The field holds more hold-up horses than the race map can accommodate at the rear: Milford Grange, Black Storm, Phoenix Of Dreams, Supreme Clarets, Yaaser, Tap Dancer, and Circle Of Trust are all natural hold-up types, but the majority will be forced to race in midfield or closer than ideal, with only the most tractable truly able to settle deep. Highfield Viking, carrying prominent-racing credentials, is the profile this race shape most directly rewards — a horse able to sit a length or two off the contested front pair, travel within himself, and pick off the leaders once Runninsonofagun and Sanafi Zabeel have had their duel, represents the sweet spot in this pace scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Runninsonofagun and Sanafi Zabeel push each other hard early and burn off at a true gallop, the race sets up perfectly for the horse sitting a length off in third or fourth.
scenarios.body: Highfield Viking, travelling prominently just behind the contested front pair, can use his class at 7f on Good ground to quicken once the pace horses tie each other up entering the final two furlongs; this scenario rewards horses who race efficiently without expending energy in the early exchanges.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leaders Sustain, Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-running pair — most likely Runninsonofagun — manages to control the pace slightly and steal a length-and-a-half margin without being fully pressed, the leader can sustain that advantage.
scenarios.body: Runninsonofagun has the form figures on Good ground and his recent course-and-distance profile suggests he handles a true gallop, so if Sanafi Zabeel cannot sustain pressure beyond the halfway point, the leader can coast clear; this scenario is most likely if Sanafi Zabeel over-races early and weakens.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Storm Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so fierce that it completely collapses the front pair and the field spreads wide entering the straight, creating space for the deepest runners to find a line.
scenarios.body: Several genuine hold-up types will be racing out of their natural rhythm, but Black Storm and Circle Of Trust have the form profiles to still arrive late if the race falls apart at the front; this scenario is structurally less likely given how many supposed hold-up horses are forced to race mid-division and will not be in true hold-up positions.

watchPoints.text: Runninsonofagun and Sanafi Zabeel will fight for the early lead from the gates — watch whether either blinks first before halfway, as the one who does risks emptying before the straight and gifting the race to Highfield Viking.

Phoenix Of Dreams has had 102 days off the track and has exclusively run on Standard going in recent starts — if the Good turf surface is genuinely quicker than he has encountered in 2025, watch for him to fail to travel with his usual fluency.

Circle Of Trust's form on Good ground is a concern — two runs on Good produced a 9th and 10th place, suggesting the surface blunts his effectiveness despite his hold-up style looking theoretically suited to a pace-duel race shape.

Yy Spirit's 99-day absence combined with a 7lb claim from Lexie Clarkson creates an information gap — watch how she jumps and settles in the first furlong; if she is free or slow to begin, her chance will evaporate quickly in this pace-pressured race.

The cluster of Jim Goldie runners (Sanafi Zabeel, Yaaser, Tap Dancer) means the stable has multiple interests — watch whether Sanafi Zabeel is ridden to lead genuinely or if pace is manufactured to suit one of the stable's hold-up companions.

races.name: Festive Day Dancing At Ayr Racecourse Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Wicklow Way
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Soft/All-Weather and has placed at 8-10f on Good; hold-up style suits a strong pace but this controlled tempo and a crowded rear makes getting a clear run the key concern for Jack Garritty.

runners_data.name: Charencey
runners_data.note: Two consecutive second-place finishes at 10-12f on Good ground give this six-year-old strong course-condition credentials; races from hold-up, so Ryan Kavanagh will need to navigate through a packed field, though the form profile is among the most relevant in the race.

runners_data.name: Falaise Blanc
runners_data.note: Consistent placed horse at 12-13f on Good turf — four places from five recent starts at that trip — and her prominent style (mapped accurately here) means Jake Dickson can avoid the rear-group traffic and fire off a straightforward challenge; headgear (blinkers) adds a concentration angle.

runners_data.name: Golden Valour
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old who carries a genuine win at 10f on Good; his true racing style is hold-up, though the crowded map has him showing in midfield — at his age and this OR, he needs things to fall perfectly and the style compromise is a real cost.

runners_data.name: One More Bottle
runners_data.note: Modest recent form (0-8-7 last three runs) and has spent most of his career racing on All-Weather rather than turf; a natural hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield slot he won't occupy willingly, and Barry McHugh faces a stiff task coaxing him into contention.

runners_data.name: Patrick Street
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Good and has a record of placing at various stamina trips; races hold-up, but his form string includes a recent good effort and M.P. Sheehy can look to exploit the steady pace if he can get a clear passage from the rear-group tangle.

runners_data.name: Sassy Glory
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner, wearing a visor, and Jason Hart simply has to slot her into the lead and manage the tempo — her second in a 10f Good-ground race and previous win at 8f suggest she has enough quality to hold on if the race is truly run to suit her.

runners_data.name: Storm On Jura
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in finishes and holds a true hold-up profile that is displaced to midfield on the map; Lauren Young (claimer) faces a tactical puzzle in a crowded field, and the fade warning over 10-12f on Good is a genuine negative at this distance.

runners_data.name: Zebra Star
runners_data.note: A six-year-old who has placed at 10f on Soft and has decent Good-going exposure, though without a win; genuine hold-up racer shown in midfield here, and Shay Farmer (claimer) will need to find daylight from a position he is unlikely to naturally occupy.

runners_data.name: Flying Moonlight
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with back-to-back third-place finishes at 8f on Good/Soft; his true nature is hold-up and he is younger and lightly raced, so Sean Kirrane will hope for a trouble-free passage, but the step up in field size and OR level is a challenge.

runners_data.name: Raise The Stakes
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish warning noted, but has placed twice at 10f on Good ground recently; hold-up racer who needs a genuinely run race to land a blow, and with 43 days off the track, fitness is a secondary query even if the trip and going are fine.

runners_data.name: Resdev Time
runners_data.note: Three-year-old in fair form (six runs, twice placed at 12f on Good); a hold-up horse mapped to midfield because the rear is overloaded — Billy Garritty will need to find a way through in the straight, and the Michael & David Easterby yard has had some recent runners.

runners_data.name: Sanny Doo
runners_data.note: Lowest OR in the field (43) and has not placed in any of his last five runs; a hold-up type shown in midfield due to redistribution, and Paul Mulrennan faces the dual challenge of an out-of-role map position and the weakest rating in the race.

races.paceDynamic: Sassy Glory is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to press her hard from the gates, she should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 1m2f trip on Good ground at Ayr. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types — Charencey, Wicklow Way, Raise The Stakes, Falaise Blanc and Patrick Street among the more credible closers — meaning the chasing pack will be stacked in a dense, traffic-heavy group behind her. The field holds significantly more hold-up and prominent types than the race map can accommodate naturally; One More Bottle, Storm On Jura, Resdev Time, Sanny Doo, Flying Moonlight, Zebra Star and Golden Valour are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield positions they will not truly occupy by choice, making the mid-to-rear section genuinely congested. With a lone leader setting a measured tempo and a wall of closers queuing behind, this race shape most strongly favours horses who can race handy or in a prominent position just off the pace — runners who can avoid the traffic and strike without needing a sustained late sprint from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sassy Glory Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Sassy Glory gets a clean lead and no rival has the natural pace or inclination to press her, setting a comfortable tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Sassy Glory controls the race from the front at a measured pace that plays to her stamina, and horses that can travel just behind her without being buried in the pack are best placed to challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travels prominently just off Sassy Glory's pace and produces a timely challenge turning for home.
scenarios.body: The controlled gallop set by Sassy Glory invites a prominent tracker to sit within two lengths throughout and kick past in the final furlong; Falaise Blanc's consistent placed form at 12-13f on Good ground makes her the natural beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently in the straight to cause the prominent horses to tie up, opening a path for a strong finisher from the rear.
scenarios.body: A true hold-up horse who can find clean daylight through a congested field — Raise The Stakes and Charencey both have recent placed form at this sort of trip on Good — could pick off tiring rivals late, though traffic in a large field on this track makes this scenario genuinely difficult to execute.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sassy Glory Wins Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly crawling and Sassy Glory's rivals are all too far back to reel her in after she quickens entering the straight.
scenarios.body: With most of the field needing a genuine gallop to bring their finishing kick into play, an extremely slow pace paradoxically benefits the front-runner who simply slows rivals' momentum out of the back straight and sprints clear before closers can mobilise.

watchPoints.text: Sassy Glory (Jason Hart) is the only front-runner in a 13-horse field — watch whether any of the prominent types attempt to dispute the lead early, as any pressure on her could fundamentally change the race shape.

The redistribution of seven genuine hold-up horses into midfield map positions means the rear-to-mid section will be genuinely congested; watch for traffic trouble and interference in the straight, particularly affecting Resdev Time, Storm On Jura and Sanny Doo.
Raise The Stakes is flagged as fading in the finish and has had 43 days off the track — if Greg Fairley commits too early from hold-up, the fade warning may prove costly in the final furlong.

Falaise Blanc's blinkers (first-time or re-applied) merit monitoring at the start — if she jumps cleanly and takes her natural prominent position, she is best-placed tactically in the entire field given how the pace map shapes up.

Storm On Jura (33 days off, fades in finish, claimer Lauren Young) represents a compounded risk cluster — layoff, stamina question and inexperienced pilot combine to make her the most vulnerable runner if the race quickens before the final furlong.
